Sun, 26 Jul 2026 14:07:54 +0000 en-US hourly 1 https://wordpress.org/?v=7.0.4 https://beesayatv.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/cropped-09-32x32.png Out and Back – beesayatv https://beesayatv.com/ 32 32 Cambanog Falls | Dumanjug | 2026 GPX https://beesayatv.com/trails/cambanog-falls-dumanjug-2026-gpx/ Wed, 01 Jul 2026 07:20:43 +0000 https://beesayatv.com/?post_type=trail&p=414 Cambanog Falls is a documented 2 km out-and-back hike in Langin, Kambanog, Dumanjug. I followed a short trail that descended through open terrain toward the river before returning along the same route. Although the approach was mostly downhill, the lower sections included a few uneven areas and short climbs before the continuous uphill walk back to the jump-off. I completed this hike in April 2026.

Trail Snapshot

EASY
DocumentedApril 2026
Distance~2 km (Out and Back)
Elevation Gain51 m
Duration15-30 mins
WaterAt least 1 liter
ShadeNone
Surface100% trail
GPXWikiloc

Forecast data: Open-Meteo

Access

I started near Cambanog Elementary School, where motorcycle parking was available along the roadside without a parking fee. The jump-off was accessible by a rough road, and private vehicles could reach the area. Public transportation was limited, although habal-habal services were available.

Why this trail is rated Easy

✓ Easy-to-follow trail
✓ No technical climbing required
✓ Short hiking distance
✓ Mostly downhill route
✓ River crossings are manageable during normal conditions

On this trail: river crossing • waterfall

Route Description

I began by descending toward the river on a trail that was easy to follow. The upper section gradually lost elevation before reaching a few uneven stretches and short climbs closer to the water. After reaching Cambanog Falls, I retraced the same route back to the starting point.

The return consisted of a steady uphill climb from the river to the jump-off. Even though the overall distance was short, the climb out required more effort than the approach.

Trail Conditions

The weather remained sunny throughout my hike. Most of the route was exposed with limited shade, while the trail stayed dry during my visit. Walking conditions could become muddy after rain. I found a few stores near the route, and mobile signal remained strong near the jump-off before disappearing near the river.

Additional Notes

The trail surface is mostly soil from the jump-off point to the river and can become very muddy after rain.

]]> Mt. Kalatkat | Sayao, Sibonga | 2026 GPX https://beesayatv.com/trails/kalatkat-trail/ Thu, 25 Jun 2026 10:24:49 +0000 https://beesayatv.com/?post_type=trail&p=221 Mt. Kalatkat is a documented 3.5 km out-and-back hike in Kalangyawon, Sayao, Sibonga. I started near Kalangyawon Elementary School and followed a gradual climb through grassy mountain slopes and narrow livestock paths before returning along the same route.

The trail was easy to follow throughout and remained a straightforward walk with little technical difficulty. I completed this hike in May 2026 under sunny morning conditions.

Trail Snapshot

EASY
DocumentedMay 2026
Distance3.5 km (Out and Back)
Elevation Gain184 m
Duration1-2 hrs
WaterAt least 1 liter
ShadeLimited
Surface30% trail, 70% road
GPXWikiloc

Forecast data: Open-Meteo

Access

I started near Kalangyawon Elementary School, where motorcycle parking was available along the roadside without a parking fee. The jump-off was accessible by a mix of paved and concrete roads, and private vehicles could reach the area. There was no public transportation available, although habal-habal services operated nearby. Motorcycles could also continue near the foot of the mountain, but I chose to begin at the school for a longer approach.

Why this trail is rated Easy

✓ Easy-to-follow trail
✓ Communities located along the route
✓ No dangerous cliff exposure
✓ Suitable for first-time solo hikers
✓ Short hiking distance

On this trail: cliff • peak

Route Description

I began by walking through the community before the trail gradually climbed across grassy hillsides. Narrow footpaths used by local livestock led toward the summit, and navigation remained simple from start to finish. After reaching Mt. Kalatkat, I retraced the same route back to the jump-off.

Trail Conditions

The weather stayed sunny throughout my hike. Most of the lower sections were shaded, while the trail became more exposed as I approached the summit. The ground remained dry during my visit, and I did not find any stores along the route. Mobile signal was intermittent, the trail was quiet with very few other people around, and I only noticed a small number of insects.

Additional Notes

The trail was well-trodden because locals regularly used it to move livestock through the area. Starting from Kalangyawon Elementary School added extra walking distance, although motorcycles could reach the foot of the mountain and shorten the hike considerably.

]]> Malingin Rock | Cotcot River, Liloan | 2026 GPX https://beesayatv.com/trails/malingin-rock/ Thu, 25 Jun 2026 10:15:41 +0000 https://beesayatv.com/?post_type=trail&p=213 Malingin Rock is a documented 1.5 km out-and-back hike in Mulao, Liloan, leading to the Cotcot River. I followed a straightforward trail that descended through farms before reaching the river, then returned along the same route with a short but steeper uphill climb back to the jump-off.

Navigation remained simple throughout the hike, making the route easy to follow from start to finish. I completed this hike in May 2026.

Trail Snapshot

EASY
DocumentedMay 2026
Distance1.5 km (Out and Back)
Elevation Gain106 m
Duration2 hrs
WaterAt least 1 liter
ShadeLimited
Surface100% trail
GPXWikiloc

Forecast data: Open-Meteo

Access

I started near Mulao Barangay Hall, where motorcycle parking was available along the roadside without a parking fee. The jump-off was accessible by concrete road, and private vehicles could reach the area. There was no public transportation serving the trailhead, although habal-habal services were available. From Liloan proper, the drive to the jump-off covered about 11 km.

Why this trail is rated Easy

✓ Easy-to-follow trail
✓ Straightforward navigation
✓ Short hiking distance
✓ No technical climbing required
✓ Suitable for first-time solo hikers

On this trail: river crossing • rock formation

Route Description

I began by descending through small farmlands toward the Cotcot River. The trail was easy to follow and gradually led downhill until I reached Malingin Rock. After spending time at the river, I retraced my steps back to the starting point. Although the hike was short, the return climb felt more tiring because it was entirely uphill.

Trail Conditions

The weather was sunny during my hike, and the trail remained dry throughout. Most of the route was shaded, although the riverside sections were more exposed. I found stores only at the jump-off, while mobile signal was strong near the start before becoming weaker closer to the river. I did not encounter other hikers, and insects were minimal.

Additional Notes

Some residents along the access road raised pigs, and I noticed occasional livestock odors before reaching the jump-off. I also noted that Malingin Rock had shifted downstream by approximately 11 meters following Typhoon Odette and Typhoon Tino. During my visit, it was much closer to the trail exit leading to the river than its previous location.
